## Learn from real films, credit the people who made them

The fastest way to get better at motion is to study films people loved: the launch video everyone shared, the ad you watched three times. With v1.4 the kit gives you a way to do that openly. You bring real videos as references, measure what makes them work, borrow the grammar, and **name the people you learned from**, in the repo and when you post.

### The rule
**Every reference is credited by name and link, and only grammar is borrowed. Never assets.**

| Borrow (grammar) | Don't take (assets) |
|---|---|
| Rhythm: cuts per 10 s, how fast the first 3 s go, where the hold is | Their footage, frames or screen recordings |
| Structure: hook → reveal → proof → CTA, where the surprise sits | Their music, sound design or voice-over |
| A transition *type*, such as a match cut on a shape or a whip into a UI | Their characters, mascots, logos or copy |
| A camera idea, such as an over-the-shoulder dive or a dolly-out reveal | A signature look so close it could pass for theirs |

The full guide is in [`creative/references.md`](https://github.com/tugrawork-creator/saas-motion-kit/blob/main/creative/references.md).

### `tools/breakdown.py`: a reference, broken into shots
```bash
python tools/breakdown.py launch.mp4 --id 01 --creator "@handle" --title "v2 launch" --url https://x.com/handle/status/…
```
It finds the hard cuts and measures the rhythm: cuts per 10 s, median, shortest and longest shot, and how many cuts land in the first 3 s. It also writes a contact sheet with one frame per shot and a draft ledger in the storyboard format. Every breakdown opens with the creator's name and link. The output goes to the git-ignored `.references/` folder, so other people's work never ends up in your repo.

### Credit you can't forget
1. **`REFERENCES.md`** sits next to the storyboard, with one row per reference: creator, title, link, what you borrowed and what you didn't. Start from [the template](https://github.com/tugrawork-creator/saas-motion-kit/blob/main/templates/REFERENCES.md).
2. **`ref:01`** goes in the ledger notes of every shot that borrows from that reference. `variety_audit.py`, and the GitHub Action with it, now **fails** when a `ref:` has no credited row with a creator and a link.
3. **When you post**, add a credit line such as "Rhythm inspired by @handle's launch film (link). Made with saas-motion-kit." and tag them.

The `/saas-motion-video` skill now asks for reference videos at the brief.

### Fixes
- The 100 theme sheets no longer say "all 100 themes".
- `history_report.py` accepts theme ids written as numbers.
- `variety_audit.py` reports an unreadable time instead of crashing.
- `loop_check.py` and `deliver.sh` print their usage instead of a traceback when called without arguments.

Full notes: [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/tugrawork-creator/saas-motion-kit/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

---

**TR:** v1.4 ile sevdiğin gerçek videoları referans olarak kullanabiliyorsun: herkesin paylaştığı lansman filmlerini ya da üç kez izlediğin reklamları. Kural basit: her referans, yaratıcısının adı ve linkiyle anılır ve yalnızca dil ödünç alınır (ritim, yapı, geçiş türü, kamera fikri). Görüntü, müzik, karakter, logo ya da metin asla alınmaz. `tools/breakdown.py` bir videoyu çekimlerine ayırıp ritmini ölçüyor ve sonucu kredi başlığıyla git'e girmeyen bir klasöre yazıyor. Storyboard'da `ref:01` gibi bir işaret kullandığında, yanındaki `REFERENCES.md`'de bir yaratıcı adı ve bir link yoksa audit hata veriyor. Paylaşırken de onları etiketle; insanlar işlerinden birinin bir şey öğrendiğini duymayı sever. Bu sürümde birkaç hata düzeltmesi de var.
